label: b46: c51 screen -- batch 512, soft target, 21 / 201 atoms (seed 2, vs b38b)
notes:
THIS ARM: 51 atoms -> 21, over the same support [-5, 120]. Atom spacing goes 2.50 -> 6.25.

WHY. 51 is the number in the C51 paper, chosen on Atari returns, and nothing in this project has ever
tested it. This arm and b46d bracket it, so between them they answer whether the resolution is wrong at
all before anyone tunes it. The case for FEWER is statistical: each atom's probability is estimated from
the same stream of transitions, so 21 atoms means ~2.4x the effective data per atom and a smaller
softmax to fit, which is the same variance argument as b46a arriving by a different route. The case
against is that the support has to represent this domain's returns, and at DISCOUNT=0.9975 with a
PERFECT_GAME_REWARD of 100 those returns are concentrated near the top of the range -- coarser bins may
blur exactly the distinctions that matter near a win.

WHAT TO WATCH FOR THAT IS NOT THE SCORE. A coarser support cannot represent a bimodal 'win or die'
value distribution as sharply, so if this arm's score holds while its churn falls, the resolution was
buying nothing and costing stability. The reverse -- score falls, churn falls -- means the atoms were
load-bearing and 21 threw away real information.

V_MIN AND V_MAX ARE DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, in this arm and in b46d. The support's RANGE has to match
the returns the reward function can produce, and that is a property of the environment, not of the atom
count; moving it would confound resolution with coverage and make both arms unreadable. Note also that
V_MAX is not freely tunable here for a second reason -- CLAUDE.md's rule is that it must be re-derived
from the reward scale rather than scaled, and this config's -5/120 is that derivation for
PERFECT_GAME_REWARD=100 at DISCOUNT=0.9975.

THE BATCH. Four one-knob variants of b38's c51 config, one seed, 3M steps, measured against
b38b-c51fc320eps3125seed2 as the matched control. b38's own four arms are the noise estimate: at 3M
they pooled 78.51 / 71.79 / 72.53 / 72.66 (spread 6.7 pp) with strong_eval_fraction 31.0 / -- / 18.6 /
22.2. So a single arm has to move pooled by MORE than ~7 pp before its own seed stops being the
likelier explanation, and NO arm of this batch is to be called a win on its score alone. Read churn
(perDiagnostics/c51_stability.py) as the primary signal -- it resolved a ~4x effect on a pair where
n=2 score could not -- and treat score as the confirmation.

WHY BUILD OFF b38 AND NOT b36. Both are the same config apart from Adam epsilon (b36 1.5e-4, b38
3.125e-4) and that dose is closed: sign test p = 0.625, no effect. b38 is the batch that ran to the
full 3.00M cap on all four arms, while b36 was stopped at 1.87-2.02M -- so at the 3M horizon these
arms are capped at, b38 is the only exact 4-seed control that exists. Choosing it costs nothing and
buys a real baseline.

WHY SEED 2. b38b is the arm with the largest unambiguous defect that is still clearly learning: the
highest best_perfect30 of either batch (88.3%) on the LOWEST pooled (71.79%), with trailing falling
81.2 -> 74.6 over its last 700k steps. That is a policy that reaches a good place and cannot hold it,
which is precisely the failure every arm here is aimed at, and it leaves headroom in the metric that
a seed-1-style control would not. All four arms share seed 2 so they are comparable to each other as
well as to b38b.

WHAT THE WHOLE BATCH IS ABOUT. c51 has underperformed the scalar arms across b36/b38 and the
suspicion is that the shortfall is in the LOSS, not the algorithm: a categorical head learns a
distribution over 51 atoms from the same single transition a scalar head uses for one number, and the
projected Bellman target is rebuilt from a target network that jumps discontinuously across the whole
support every 1000 steps. Arms a and b attack the gradient's noise and the target's smoothness; arms
c and d ask whether 51 atoms is the wrong resolution in either direction. If all four land inside
b38's seed spread, the shortfall is not in these knobs and the next place to look is the priority
signal (kl vs ce) or C51_DOUBLE.

WHAT THIS BATCH IS NOT. Not a HOF attempt -- 3M from scratch does not reach the >=98% band, so expect
auto_hof to exit `done` with nothing measured, which is normal. Judge on strong_eval_fraction, banded
mean perfect rate and the close-out's pooled figure, NOT on peak_trailing (trailing average SCORE,
which saturates at 95/95 for any arm that fills a board).

MEASUREMENT ERA. These are batch-45-onward arms: graph evals are 20 episodes, so perfect_percent comes
in multiples of 5 rather than 10. best_perfect30 and max_single_eval are maxima over a noisy statistic
and are biased DOWN relative to b36/b38's 10-episode era -- do not compare those two metrics across
the boundary. The close-out runs on the vectorised engine, which is flat and ungated, so its rows carry
min_achievable: null and are directly poolable; b38's rows were gated at 95, so compare pooled figures
only via the graph-100% tier or by re-reading the gate in each payload.
